newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds fade marginally, issuance expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds fade marginally, issuance expected.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds marked time on Monday, leaving prices to fade with Treasuries ahead of an expected resurgence of investment grade and high-yield supply, dealers across both markets said.

Mounting new issuance is expected to take center stage this week as companies rush to capitalize on sharply lower borrowing rates ahead, syndicate officials said. Firms will also move to tackle fourth quarter capital needs, they said.
"It's a positive issuing environment...I suspect there's going to be a lot of issuance in the next few weeks," said one syndicate official.

But while the buzz of heavier issuance was heard throughout the Street on Monday, only one large high-grade issue came to market. Smith Barney Holdings issued $200 million 7.125 percent 10-year notes to yield 7.188 percent, or 68 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve. The deal is rated A2/A-minus and was led by Smith Barney Inc.

Some new issues widened substantially when freed to trade, dealers said, reflecting mispricing more than market weakness. At least one trader said the onset of fresh paper kept the lid on bidding for the paper on Monday, however.

In secondary trade, Travelers/Aetna Property & Casualty Co's $200 million three-year A2/single-A three-year notes were quoted behind 30 basis points over U.S. Treasuries compared with the original issue spread of 25 basis points. Smith Barney Inc was lead manager on the deal.

Norwest Corp's $200 million AA3/AA-minus 10-year senior notes also sought equilibrium when freed, widening nine basis points on the bid side. The notes were quoted at 49 basis point bid, 47 offer at midday versus the original issue spread of 40 basis points.
Still, most paper merely followed softening Treasuries.

Looking ahead, the News Corporation said it filed a shelf registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for up to $1.0 billion in debt securities. The company said proceeds will be added to its general funds and will be used for working capital and other corporate purposes.
High-yielders also sustained marginal losses on Monday due to generally lackluster trade, dealers said. The broad market was estimated down 1/8 point, they added.
New junk issues traded higher, but without the verve experienced over the past several weeks. New issuance will test the state of the "overheated" market, traders said.

"There's quite a bit of paper that's supposed to come this week and guys are waiting to see if the trend continues," one high-yield trader said. "But it died out Friday afternoon, it's dead today, so today its hard to tell."

All American Communications $100 million B3/B-minus senior subordinated notes settled back to a 100-1/2 bid near the close after trading as high as 101, one trader said. The notes were offered at 101-3/8 in the aftermarket on Friday.

Mettler Toledo's $135 million B1/single-B 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced at par on Friday to yield 9.75 percent, were quoted at 101-3/4 bid late on Monday. The notes were offered at 102-1/4 by the close on Friday.

Junk issuance will feature $350 million in debt from Paging Network Inc, $225 million notes from Goss Graphic Systems, and $150 million senior subordinated notes from Outdoor Systems, according to synidicate sources.
In the Treasury market, prices faded on profit-taking ahead of new government supply and the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 15/32 at 99-16/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
